newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ISRAEL PRIVATE CAPITAL INFOWS UP IN 1997.
newsitem.headline: ISRAEL PRIVATE CAPITAL INFOWS UP IN 1997.

text.p: Private capital inflows to Israel rose to $6.6 billion in the first half of 1997 against $5.1 billion in all of 1996, the Bank of Israel said on Wednesday.
"The rise in capital inflows stems mainly from the growth in credit taken by Israeli citizens from local banks denominated in foreign currencies," the central bank said in a statement.
It said Israelis had increased foreign currency credit in the first six months of 1997 to $4 billion against $2.2 billion in all of 1996.
High shekel interest rates prompted Israeli businesses to turn to foreign currency loans.
The central bank said foreign investment remained high in the first half of 1997 at $1.5 billion but that the composition of foreign holdings in Israel had changed.
The bank said foreign portfolio investment on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange had grown markedly to $500 million since the start of the year against $340 million for all of 1996.
It said direct foreign investment and holdings of Israeli shares abroad had fallen.
